ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Republic of the Marshall Islands Business Corporations Act 1990, as amended (P.L. 1990-52, 31 MIRC 101 et seq.); Non-Resident Domestic Corporation Act (31 MIRC 401 et seq.); Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing Act 2005, as amended (38 MIRC 101 et seq.); Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing (Customer Due Diligence) Regulations 2006; Banks and Trust Companies Act 2000, as amended (governing licensed registered agents); Financial Intelligence Unit Guidelines 2017. UBO records are maintained privately by the registered agent and must be produced to the Financial Intelligence Unit upon request; no public UBO register exists.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Corporate Existence / Good Standing of any foreign corporate shareholder or parent entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Filing authority or Companies Registry in the entity's country of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or, if non-Hague country, Consular Legalization at an RMI Embassy or Consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of the board resolution approving incorporation of the Marshall Islands Business Corporation and the authorised signatories
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the jurisdiction where the resolution is executed

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized certificate identifying all ultimate beneficial owners holding directly or indirectly 25% or more interest
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public / designated AML compliance officer of the applicant

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney appointing the resident agent and/or registered agent of the Marshall Islands Business Corporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the principal's jurisdiction

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All directors, officers, shareholders, ultimate beneficial owners, and material transaction counterparties must be screened in real time against the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, U.S. OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, UK HM Treasury Consolidated List, and the RMI Financial Intelligence Unit's domestic list. PEP status is verified using a commercial AML database updated at least daily; enhanced due diligence applies to any PEP, significant domestic official, or high-risk individual. All screening results must be documented and retained for at least five years.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Marshall Islands Corporate Registry Portal (Office of the Commerce Registrar, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Trade)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be submitted in the English or Latin alphabet. Marshallese words are permitted only in Latin transliteration. The name must contain a statutory corporate suffix: Corporation, Incorporated, Company, Limited, or a recognized abbreviation such as Corp., Inc., Co., or Ltd. The name must be distinguishable from all existing registered names and must not include characters outside A-Z, 0-9, ampersand, apostrophe, hyphen, or full stop.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: An applicant may appeal a name rejection by delivering a written request for reconsideration to the Office of the Commerce Registrar within 14 calendar days of the rejection notice. The request must set out the legal bases for appeal and may include amended name options. The Registrar must issue a written determination within 21 business days. If the rejection is upheld, the applicant may seek judicial review in the High Court of the Republic of the Marshall Islands under the Administrative Procedure Act (Chapter 3 of Title 5 MIRC) within 30 days of the final administrative decision.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office is permissible for a non-resident Business Corporation engaged solely in offshore bitumen/asphalt wholesale trading, provided a licensed registered agent maintains a physical registered office in Majuro and accepts service of process. No local employees, warehouse, or business premises are mandatory for the non-resident enterprise.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 3% annual probability of unannounced inspection of the registered agent's office by the Office of the Commerce Registrar; less than 1% for a fully offshore commercial substance profile, but the registered agent's premises remain subject to AML/CFT inspection.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name reservation and availability clearance fee
Articles of Incorporation filing fee (no minimum capital; standard multi-class share authorization)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff based on authorized shares

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Annual registered agent fee (including physical registered office and corporate records access)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for non-resident corporations

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO, AML, KYC, PEP and sanctions screening per ultimate beneficial owner
Notarization, apostille or consular legalization of corporate charter and incumbency bundle
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Applicable statutory fee schedule of the certification country

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Pre-incorporation corporate legal counsel fee (drafting, review and filing)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market hourly rate (blended, estimated 3 hours)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance thresholds for wastewater, VOCs, or waste handling

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Revenue and Taxation Division, Ministry of Finance, Republic of the Marshall Islands; corporate registry authority: Office of the Registrar of Corporations (Majuro); filings are executed through licensed registered agents via paper submission, with no fully digitized national tax portal.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A non-resident Business Corporation is formed by filing Articles of Incorporation under the Marshall Islands Business Corporations Act and obtaining the Certificate of Incorporation. The entity then files the Business License Application and pays the annual Business License Tax. Upon issuance of the license, the Revenue and Taxation Division registers the entity and assigns a Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN). No income tax registration or return obligation arises where the BC has no RMI-source income and conducts no business within Marshall Islands territory.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box election comparable to IRC Section 7701 exists, and no hybrid mismatch election is available under RMI law. Taxation follows a source-of-income model: the non-resident BC is taxable only on RMI-source gross receipts; income derived from offshore wholesale trading of containerized bitumen falls outside the RMI tax net provided the corporation maintains non-resident status and does not transact business in the RMI.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: No VAT or GST regime in force; indirect taxation consists exclusively of Import Duty under the RMI Customs Tariff and the flat-rate Business License Tax under the Business License Act.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Not applicable — no VAT/GST or economic turnover threshold exists. A flat annual Business License Tax of approximately USD 100–300 applies regardless of gross turnover; the RMI operates on the United States Dollar as legal tender.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: None — the Marshall Islands mandates no real-time fiscal clearance platform, no electronic invoicing API requirement, and no digital tax stamping or e-invoice telemetry. Exporters rely on paper-based commercial documentation retained for customs and tax audit purposes.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Not applicable — RMI imposes no VAT/GST, hence no export zero-rating or refund mechanism exists. Exported containerized penetration-grade bitumen nonetheless qualifies for customs duty exemption on export and remains outside the RMI gross-receipts tax base where: (i) title and risk of loss pass to the foreign buyer outside RMI; (ii) the goods are shipped from an RMI port to a foreign destination; and (iii) the seller is a non-resident Business Corporation with no RMI trading presence.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration filed under the RMI Customs Act
Ocean Bill of Lading or Sea Waybill evidencing the containerized shipment
Container packing list and containerized cargo manifest
Commercial invoice stating INCOTERMS and foreign destination
Inward Remittance Certificate or SWIFT MT103 evidencing USD payment and FX repatriation
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: No VAT zero-rating clawback is available by design; the operative audit risk is mischaracterization of RMI-source income as foreign-source. Under the RMI Income Tax Act 1989, negligence or failure to file attracts penalties up to 25% of the underpaid tax plus interest at 1% per month; fraudulent returns expose directors to criminal fines and imprisonment under the RMI Criminal Code; and false customs export declarations may result in seizure, forfeiture, and monetary penalties under the Customs Act.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: The Republic of the Marshall Islands does not establish a central bank and maintains no domestic foreign exchange administration. The U.S. dollar is the legal tender and national currency. Banking supervision and licensing are administered by the Banking Commissioner / Office of the Banking Commissioner within the Ministry of Finance. In practice, monetary stability and dollar clearing are functions of the U.S. Federal Reserve System and the U.S. dollar correspondent banking network.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Marshall Islands operates a fully dollarized monetary system with no statutory exchange controls. Both current account and capital account transactions are freely convertible for practical purposes because the monetary unit is the U.S. dollar and no domestic exchange control legislation restricting conversion exists. Profit remittance, dividend distribution, capital repatriation, and trade settlement are not subject to central bank approval or FX licensing. The only practical hurdles are bank-level AML/KYC clearance, OFAC sanctions screening, and correspondent bank restrictions. Non-resident business corporations may hold and disburse USD freely, and no RMI tax or exchange control charge is imposed on profit remittance.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There are no statutory export proceeds surrender timelines and no mandatory conversion ratios in the Republic of the Marshall Islands. Since the U.S. dollar is both the domestic currency and the export invoicing currency, export receipts may be retained in USD, credited to the exporter's operational account, and used for any lawful purpose. The exporter is not required to repatriate, convert, or surrender proceeds to a central bank or official counterparty. The only compliance duties arise from correspondent bank screening, OFAC/sanctions checks, and the bank's internal transaction monitoring framework.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Operational USD Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Operational USD Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Low. Offshore digital EMI and virtual-account platforms are not recognized as licensed deposit-taking institutions under the Marshall Islands Banking Act framework. Only entities holding a valid banking licence in the Republic, or domestic registered agents acting as introducers, may provide account or payment services to an RMI corporate entity. An offshore EMI may not lawfully maintain a bank account or hold client funds as a RMI bank. Cross-border digital EMIs are therefore best used only as payment gateways or prepaid collection tools, not as primary treasury accounts, and only where their licensing in another recognised jurisdiction is verified.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is generally required for account opening approval under domestic bank policies applying RMI AML/CFT regulations and the U.S. correspondent banking rules. Authorised signatories and ultimate beneficial owners should expect an in-person interview at the bank's Majuro or designated branch. Remote onboarding may be considered on a discretionary basis, but only with a licensed registered agent, notarised and apostilled KYC documentation, independent director verification, and a live video interview. For a purely non-resident Business Corporation, the most reliable route is a physical onboarding visit by at least one director and the beneficial owner or a personally verified attorney-in-fact.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident shell structure with no physical RMI office and no local substance evidence.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate of Good Standing, Central Registry extract, registered agent certificate, directors and ultimate beneficial owner register, economic substance explanation, contract evidence showing real commodity trading activity, corporate bank reference, and audited or management financial statements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear source of funds or unexplained large inbound capital injection.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board resolution authorising capital contribution, subscription or capital contribution agreement, source-of-wealth statement, bank statements of the remitting investor for the preceding 12 months, tax or tax-exemption status confirmation, and notarised identification documents for all signatories.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade-based money laundering concern from commodity invoicing or third-party settlement.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Commercial contract, proforma invoice and final invoice, bill of lading, packing list, container list, independent quantity/quality inspection certificate, insurance certificate, customs entry evidence, and matching shipping and payment records to substantiate the bitumen/asphalt cargo trade.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions, OFAC exposure, or high-risk counterparty jurisdiction linked to bitumen supply chain.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Sanctions screening reports on all counterparties, vessel/bill of lading screening, end-user and ultimate consignee declarations, certificate of origin, route confirmation, legal counsel sanctions memorandum, and a contractual undertaking barring dealings with sanctioned parties.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing is via standard USD wire through the correspondent banking network. The remitter shall issue a SWIFT MT103 from a bank account held in the legal name of the investor or parent company. The beneficiary account is the RMI bank account of the Business Corporation. Field 70 remittance information should read 'EQUITY CONTRIBUTION' or 'SHARE CAPITAL' plus the invoice or subscription reference. No RMI Government purpose code is required, but the receiving bank will require a board resolution, payment instruction, and source-of-funds evidence. Funds must be received from a known banking institution, not through cash couriers or unlicensed money transmitters, to satisfy AML and OFAC screening. If the capital is to be held for a later registered business purpose, the bank may designate the account as a Capital Escrow Account and release funds upon delivery of the corporate registration or corporate bank account activation documents.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade settlements shall be executed via SWIFT MT103 telegraphic transfers for conventional invoice-based payments and via Commercial Letters of Credit using SWIFT MT700/MT707 for high-value, document-backed bitumen/asphalt containerised trades. USD clearing occurs over the correspondent bank network, principally through Fedwire or CHIPS connectivity. Documentary credits should include the commercial invoice, packing list, full set of clean bills of lading or multimodal transport documents, container seal numbers, certificate of quantity/quality, certificate of origin, and marine insurance certificate. For containerised drummed or bagged bitumen, split-shipment and partial-discharge terms must be expressly stated in the LC to reflect multiple container deliveries and separate payment tranches. Payments to suppliers in countries without direct USD clearance may use a confirming bank in Singapore, Hong Kong, or the United States.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Offshore deliverable FX forwards against USD for settlement currencies such as EUR, GBP, AUD, and JPY
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for restricted or illiquid currencies, including USD/CNH and other Asian emerging-market currency pairs
Cross-currency swaps (USD vs EUR or USD vs CNY) for long-duration bitumen supply contracts and fixed-price procurement
FX options and zero-cost collars used solely for hedging forecast invoice exposures and not for speculative trading

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Report (Form AR) and Annual Franchise Tax
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on the last day of the month containing the incorporation anniversary; a corporation incorporated on 15 August must file and pay on or before 31 August each year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment accrues an automatic penalty of 10% per month or part thereof of the unpaid franchise tax; continued failure to pay for three consecutive years authorizes the Registrar to administratively dissolve the corporation without further notice.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Registered Agent and Registered Office Annual Renewal (included in the Annual Report)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Concurrent with the Annual Report and Franchise Tax on the incorporation anniversary month.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: If the licensed registered agent resigns and no replacement is appointed, the Registrar may dissolve the corporation for failure to maintain statutory representation; reinstatement requires filing of a new registered agent appointment and payment of all arrears.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial Ownership Information (BOI) Annual Confirmation and AML Customer Due Diligence Refresh
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Licensed Marshall Islands registered agent (administering the confidential BOI regime under the Marshall Islands Banking Commission AML/CFT framework)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: At every incorporation anniversary as part of annual CDD, and within 14 days of any share transfer or change in beneficial ownership.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-current BOI exposes the corporation to agent deregistration, monetary penalties under the Marshall Islands AML/CFT regulations, and a flag by the Banking Commission that can lead to involuntary dissolution.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory audit for this entity. The Business Corporations Act (BCA) imposes audit obligations only on (i) issuers registered under the Marshall Islands Securities Act and (ii) corporations whose securities are listed on a recognized stock exchange. A non-resident, unlisted Business Corporation engaged in offshore bitumen/asphalt wholesale trading is not subject to any size-based or revenue-based audit threshold.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: The BCA requires maintenance of adequate accounting records that reflect transactions and financial position, but non-resident domestic corporations are not required to prepare, file, or publish financial statements. If financial statements are voluntarily prepared for lenders, LC-issuing banks, or counterparty due diligence, IFRS or US GAAP is the accepted framework.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The Marshall Islands maintains no public UBO register. Under the 2021 AML amendments, the licensed registered agent must obtain, verify, and confidentially hold current beneficial ownership information at incorporation, upon any share transfer, and on an annual refresh cycle. The agent files BOI updates with the Registrar on a non-public basis; failure to confirm UBO annually is a compliance breach, not a public filing requirement.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: $650 – $1,200 per annum for a licensed registered agent and registered office service
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: $0 mandatory; voluntary certified audit for banking or LC counterparty purposes typically ranges from $4,000 to $12,000

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% (the Republic of the Marshall Islands imposes no corporate income tax on a non-resident Business Corporation; an electing Non-Resident Domestic Corporation is exempt from all RMI income taxes).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Effective income tax rate 0%. No tax holiday or preferential deduction is required because the RMI levies no corporate income tax, capital gains tax, withholding tax, branch profits tax, or value-added tax. The only recurring public charges are the annual registration fee and the annual report fee, with no income tax computation.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: No RMI corporate income tax return is prescribed. Administrative compliance is satisfied by filing the Marshall Islands Annual Report and, where applicable, the Non-Resident Domestic Corporation (NRDC) status reconfirmation with the Office of the Registrar through a licensed resident agent.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The Annual Report must be filed on or before 30 April of each calendar year. NRDC exempt-status reconfirmation is submitted concurrently with the Annual Report.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Full registered name, registration number, incorporation date, and registered corporate type.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter 'Business Corporation (Non-Resident)' and cite the NRDC election reference; do not indicate RMI-source trading activity.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Marshall Islands registered office address and licensed registered agent contact details.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use a licensed RMI agent; no physical office, staff, or inventory in the RMI is required for non-resident status.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Names, addresses, nationalities, and identification details of each director and officer.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: List all substantive directors; nominee arrangements must be disclosed to the registered agent for AML/KYC and cannot defeat a finding of beneficial ownership.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Narrative commercial description of actual operations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State: wholesale supply of drummed and bagged penetration-grade bitumen under ISIC 4661; procurement, storage, negotiation, invoicing, and banking occur entirely outside the Marshall Islands.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Authorized and issued share capital, par value, and consideration received.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report issued shares accurately; zero or nominal paid capital combined with large letter-of-credit exposure invites beneficial-ownership and substance review.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Attestation of continued eligibility for non-resident tax-exempt status.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Confirm that the corporation has no RMI-source income, no RMI real property, and no RMI commercial operations; any breach must be notified immediately to the registered agent.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: No income tax late-filing penalty or daily surcharge exists because no income tax return is due. Late filing of the Annual Report after 30 April triggers Registrar delinquency fees, suspension of good standing, refusal to issue certificates of good standing, and, after protracted delinquency, administrative dissolution. Loss of good standing also heightens bank de-risking on trade finance and letter-of-credit facilities.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% statutory RMI withholding tax on dividends paid by a non-resident Business Corporation to any shareholder, resident or non-resident.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The Marshall Islands has no comprehensive double taxation agreement in force, so no RMI treaty claim arises for outbound dividends. If a foreign source-state withholds on the underlying bitumen-trade profit or on distributions, relief must be sought under the source state's own domestic law or treaty. The RMI tax administration will issue a Certificate of Non-Resident Tax Status / Tax Residency Certificate only upon proof of NRDC filing and economic substance; a shell company with no records cannot secure such a certificate.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: RMI statutory withholding rate on IP royalties and debt interest is 0%. Because the RMI has no income tax treaty network, there is no reduced treaty rate to elect; the relevant exposure is governed by the payer's country and any applicable foreign CFC or thin-capitalization rules.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Not applicable - the RMI prescribes no statutory Local File or Master File documentation threshold (USD accounting currency). In practice, a financing bank or source-country tax authority will expect an arm's length file for intercompany bitumen purchase/sale arrangements once annual related-party turnover exceeds USD 1,000,000.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The RMI does not impose OECD/EU-style Economic Substance Regulations on a non-resident Business Corporation. Nevertheless, international tax transparency and AML standards require meaningful board control, complete accounting records, a real bank account in a reputable financial center, and bona fide commercial contracts. A 'pure mailbox' structure is not an automatic RMI violation but is a high-risk arrangement in source-country recharacterization and bank compliance reviews.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion / Abuse of Non-Resident Domestic Corporation Exemption
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Carrying on RMI-source wholesale, warehousing, distribution, or chartering of bitumen while declaring NRDC tax-exempt status; filing false annual report attestations; concealing contracts with RMI-connected counterparties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Revocation of the NRDC tax exemption; retroactive assessment of RMI income tax on all undeclared income; interest and civil penalties up to 100% of the tax evaded; monetary fines imposed by the court; strike-off from the Register of Business Corporations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Piercing the corporate veil: directors signing false declarations are jointly and severally liable for the underpaid tax, penalties, and restitution; aggravated cases carry travel bans, asset-freezing orders, director disqualification, and imprisonment under RMI criminal tax provisions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Beneficial Ownership and Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating solely through a registered agent with no bank account, no executed bitumen supply contracts, no board minutes, no accounting records, and undisclosed nominee ownership; routing LC proceeds without commercial rationale.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial or withdrawal of good standing; refusal of Certificates of Good Standing; administrative dissolution; adverse reporting to the RMI Financial Intelligence Unit; de-risking and sudden termination of trade finance facilities.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Piercing the corporate veil: creditors and financing banks may proceed directly against directors for shadow trading; nominee directors face disqualification, civil restitution, and bans on acting as officers in the RMI or in OECD financial markets.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Issuing inflated or understated invoices for penetration-grade bitumen; misdescribing drummed or bagged asphalt as other commodities; circular payments through third-country shell payees; deliberately splitting wire transfers to avoid transaction reporting thresholds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Prosecution under the RMI Anti-Money Laundering and Proceeds of Crime Act, as amended: financial penalties, confiscation of the bitumen cargo and proceeds, and custodial sentences; the Financial Intelligence Unit may also impose administrative fines and file international disclosures to FATF counterparts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and beneficial owners are personally exposed to confiscation orders and imprisonment for money-laundering predicate offenses; using nominee directors does not shield the controlling principal from criminal liability, travel controls, or extradition requests.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Selling bitumen to a related distributor below arm's length; paying supra-commercial management fees to a connected service company; prepaying for inventory never delivered; maintaining no contemporaneous pricing documentation for LC-backed related-party transactions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The RMI itself has no domestic transfer-pricing statute, but the source-country tax authority may reassess the trading margin, deny deductions for non-arm's length management fees, impose withholding tax on disguised distributions, and apply penalties and interest up to 100% of the underpaid foreign tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Foreign anti-avoidance rules (CFC, GAAR, and beneficial ownership registers) may attribute the RMI BC's income to the ultimate controllers; directors can be held personally liable for erroneous certifications and face cross-border collection, travel bans, and director disqualification.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Sanctions and Embargo Violations in Asphalt/Bitumen Trade
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Sourcing bagged or drummed bitumen from, selling to, transshipping through, or financing from OFAC, UN, or EU sanctioned jurisdictions; using vessels on the SDN list; producing inconsistent bills of lading, certificates of origin, or cargo manifests for bitumen cargo.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Enforcement by the United States, EU, and UN member states: blocking of assets, arrest of vessels, seizure of the bitumen cargo, secondary sanctions against the RMI entity, and referral to the RMI Financial Intelligence Unit for coordinated AML action.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and beneficial owners may be designated as blocked persons, subject to travel and visa bans, freezing of personal assets, personal forfeiture of cargo and demurrage, and criminal prosecution in enforcing jurisdictions.
